fullPassage: The customer asked, “Is it fifty-five cents a yard?” while getting her handbag ready. In their town, Mr. Levering was known as an honest and principled merchant. He was proud of this reputation and believed he deserved it. The actual price was fifty cents a yard, as Mr. Levering had told her earlier, but she misunderstood him. When the lady assumed that it was fifty-five cents per yard, he immediately said, “Yes, it is.” The love of gain was strong in his mind, but when the words were uttered, a disturbing perception of something restrained him. “I need twenty yards,” the customer replied, still believing it was fifty-five cents per yard. Mr. Levering stayed silent and began measuring the fabric. “It’s a real bargain at that price,” the lady commented. “You could say that,” said Mr. Levering. “But I obtained this fabric at a low price, too.” “Twenty yards at fifty-five cents is just eleven dollars,” said the customer. She counted the money and gave it to Mr. Levering, who put it in the cash register immediately. “Send the bundle to 300 Argyle Street, please,” the lady said, smiling, as she turned away. “Wait, there’s been a slight mistake!” Mr. Levering wanted to say, but he couldn’t bring himself to. He had just taken an extra dollar from her, and that was that. Gaining money at the cost of his self-respect weighed heavily on him. The burden of that dollar felt like a heavy stone dragging him down. He tried to rationalize it, but the guilt stuck with him. It affected his mood at home with his wife and kids, even though they usually brought him joy. “What’s wrong, dear? Does your head ache?” his wife inquired, concerned about his unusually silent night. “I’m fine,” he said, forcing a smile. “Pa,” his son excitedly said, “Eddy Jones stole a dollar at school today.” “Stole a dollar?” Mr. Levering was shocked, feeling a cold shiver. “Emma Wilson saw it all, and they found the dollar in his pocket,” his son explained. “He looked so pale, and he was crying so much. I felt bad for him. They sent for his mother, and she took him home.” “It must have been hard for his mother,” Mr. Levering said. “But even worse for such a small child,” his wife added. “He’ll always remember his crime and disgrace.” These words hit Mr. Levering hard. They made him uneasy and unable to enjoy his family’s company. He had to take a long walk to calm himself down before retiring to bed. The next day, the customer from the day before entered his store. His heart raced, thinking she realized he had overcharged her and had come to condemn him. However, she didn’t suspect anything. She actually bought more things. Giving her change back, Mr. Levering thought, “That weight shall be off my conscience,” and gave her an extra dollar. He was hoping that doing that would relieve his guilt. Unfortunately for him, she noticed the “error,” and he reluctantly took the dollar back. The dollar on his conscience was like a stain that couldn’t be washed off. Mr. Levering couldn’t shake off the guilt of his actions, even after trying to return the money. He thought of throwing it into the street, or giving it away to a homeless person, but his conscience whispered in his ear that the dollar wasn’t his to give away. That Sunday, he went to church with his family, but the only words he heard of the sermon were “dishonest dealings,” making him feel even worse. He thought of putting the dollar in the church’s donation box to ease his mind. However, he knew it wouldn’t provide lasting relief. The guilt would remain. He thought that confessing to the customer and returning her money in person would ease his mind. But doing that would be humiliating. He finally decided to send the lady an anonymous letter with the dollar enclosed and a short, vague explanation about the money. It was a bitter experience for him to have to go to such lengths to lift the burden of the dollar from his conscience. Although his debt was cleared, his actions could not be reversed, and because of that, he still gets reminded of what he did from time to time.

det.korean: ③ misunderstanding → misunderstood: 주어 she + 과거의 일이므로 과거형 동사가 필요
det.analysis:
✅ ① known: 'was known as ~(~로 알려져 있었다)'는 be + 과거분사(수동태)라서 known이 맞아요.

✅ ② deserved: 'he deserved it(그는 그럴 자격이 있다고 믿었다)'는 과거시제 동사로 맞아요.

❌ ③ misunderstanding → misunderstood: 'but she misunderstanding him'은 주어 she 뒤에 진짜 동사가 필요해요. -ing 형태는 동사 역할을 못 해요. 과거의 일이니 과거형 misunderstood(오해했다)로 고쳐야 맞아요 ←정답

✅ ④ assumed: 'the lady assumed that ~(그 부인은 ~라고 생각했다)'는 과거시제 동사로 맞아요.
det.tip: 주어(she) 뒤에는 진짜 동사가 있어야 해요. -ing만 있으면 문장이 안 돼요 → misunderstood.

det.tip: 관계대명사는 앞의 명사가 사람이면 who, 사물이면 which. 여기선 사람(Mr. Levering)이라 who.

✅ ② rationalize(합리화하다): '그는 그것을 합리화하려 했다(He tried to rationalize it)'는 죄책감을 애써 정당화하려는 문맥에 맞아요.

✅ ③ guilt(죄책감): '죄책감이 그에게 달라붙었다(the guilt stuck with him)'는 문맥에 맞아요.

❌ ④ misery → joy: 'even though they usually brought him misery'는 '비록 그들이 평소엔 그에게 비참함을 주지만'이 되어 문맥이 어긋나요. '~에도 불구하고(even though)'로 이어지려면 가족이 평소에는 '기쁨(joy)'을 주는 존재여야 자연스러워요 ←정답
det.tip: 'even though(~인데도)' 뒤에는 반대되는 좋은 내용이 와야 자연스러워요 → 가족은 평소 joy(기쁨)를 줌.

✅ ③ suspect(의심하다): 'she didn't suspect anything(그녀는 아무것도 의심하지 않았다)'은 문맥에 맞아요.

questions.passage: The customer asked, “Is it fifty-five cents a yard? ” while getting her handbag ready.  In their town, Mr.  Levering was known as an honest and principled merchant.  He was proud of this reputation and believed he deserved it.  The actual price was fifty cents a yard, as Mr.  Levering had told her earlier, but she misunderstood him.  When the lady assumed that it was fifty-five cents per yard, he immediately said, “Yes, it is. ” The love of gain was strong in his mind, but when the words were uttered, a disturbing perception of something restrained him.  “I need twenty yards,” the customer replied, still believing it was fifty-five cents per yard.  Mr.  Levering stayed silent and began measuring the fabric.  “It’s a real bargain at that price,” the lady commented.  “You could say that,” said Mr.  Levering.  “But I obtained this fabric at a low price, too. ” “Twenty yards at fifty-five cents is just eleven dollars,” said the customer.  She counted the money and gave it to Mr.  Levering, who put it in the cash register immediately.  “Send the bundle to 300 Argyle Street, please,” the lady said, smiling, as she turned away.  “Wait, there’s been a slight mistake! ” Mr.  Levering wanted to say, but he couldn’t bring himself to.  He had just taken an extra dollar from her, and that was that.  Gaining money at the cost of his self-respect weighed heavily on him.  The burden of that dollar felt like a heavy stone dragging him down.  He tried to rationalize it, but the guilt stuck with him.  It affected his mood at home with his wife and kids, even though they usually brought him joy.  “What’s wrong, dear?  Does your head ache? ” his wife inquired, concerned about his unusually silent night.  “I’m fine,” he said, forcing a smile.  “Pa,” his son excitedly said, “Eddy Jones stole a dollar at school today. ” “Stole a dollar? ” Mr.  Levering was shocked, feeling a cold shiver.  “Emma Wilson saw it all, and they found the dollar in his pocket,” his son explained.  “He looked so pale, and he was crying so much.  I felt bad for him.  They sent for his mother, and she took him home. ” “It must have been hard for his mother,” Mr.  Levering said.  “But even worse for such a small child,” his wife added.  “He’ll always remember his crime and disgrace. ” These words hit Mr.  Levering hard.  They made him uneasy and unable to enjoy his family’s company.  He had to take a long walk to calm himself down before retiring to bed.  The next day, the customer from the day before entered his store.  His heart raced, thinking she realized he had overcharged her and had come to condemn him.  However, she didn’t suspect anything.  She actually bought more things.  Giving her change back, Mr.  Levering thought, “That weight shall be off my conscience,” and gave her an extra dollar.  He was hoping that doing that would relieve his guilt.  Unfortunately for him, she noticed the “error,” and he reluctantly took the dollar back.  The dollar on his conscience was like a stain that couldn’t be washed off.  Mr.  Levering couldn’t shake off the guilt of his actions, even after trying to return the money.  He thought of throwing it into the street, or giving it away to a homeless person, but his conscience whispered in his ear that the dollar wasn’t his to give away.  That Sunday, he went to church with his family, but the only words he heard of the sermon were “dishonest dealings,” making him feel even worse.  He thought of putting the dollar in the church’s donation box to ease his mind.  However, he knew it wouldn’t provide lasting relief.  The guilt would remain.  He thought that confessing to the customer and returning her money in person would ease his mind.  But doing that would be humiliating.  He finally decided to send the lady an anonymous letter with the dollar enclosed and a short, vague explanation about the money.  It was a bitter experience for him to have to go to such lengths to lift the burden of the dollar from his conscience.  Although his debt was cleared, his actions could not be reversed, and because of that, he still gets reminded of what he did from time to time.

구문 분석:
- 여기서 It은 뒤의 'to have to go to such lengths(그렇게까지 애써야 하는 것)'를 대신 받는 가주어예요. 진짜 주어가 길어서 It을 앞에 두고 진짜 주어는 뒤로 보낸 구조예요.

- '그에게'는 for him.
- 순서: It + was + a bitter experience + for him → It was a bitter experience for him (7단어)

det.korean: 그는 방금 그녀에게서 1달러를 더 받았다
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- '그는 ~ 받았다(막 방금)'이므로 주어 He + 과거완료 had taken(막 ~했다)으로 뼈대를 세워요.
- '방금'을 뜻하는 just는 had와 taken 사이에 넣어요 → had just taken.
- '1달러를 더'는 an extra dollar, '그녀에게서'는 from her.
- 순서: He + had + just + taken + an extra dollar + from her → He had just taken an extra dollar from her (9단어)

accept: He had just taken an extra dollar from her

questions.passage: “I need twenty yards,” the customer replied, still believing it was fifty-five cents per yard.  Mr.  __________.  “It’s a real bargain at that price,” the lady commented.  “You could say that,” said Mr.  Levering.
questions.stem: 다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 [조건]에 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 영작하시오. (영어로) "Levering은 조용히 있다가 옷감을 재기 시작했다." [조건] (1) Levering, stayed, silent, and, began, measuring, the, fabric 을 모두 사용할 것 (2) 정확히 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: Levering은 조용히 있다가 옷감을 재기 시작했다
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- 주어 Levering + 첫 번째 동사 stayed silent(조용히 있었다)로 시작해요.
- and로 두 번째 동작을 이어요 → began measuring(재기 시작했다).
- 'begin + 동사ing(~하기 시작하다)'이라 began 뒤에 measuring이 와요.
- '옷감을'은 the fabric.
- 순서: Levering + stayed silent + and + began measuring + the fabric → Levering stayed silent and began measuring the fabric (8단어)
det.tip: begin + -ing = ~하기 시작하다 → began measuring. and로 두 동작(stayed, began)을 연결.

questions.wa: Levering stayed silent and began measuring the fabric
accept: Levering stayed silent and began measuring the fabric
